title: How science avoids false claims
summary: Why a dip is a candidate, not a discovery, what it takes to confirm a planet, and a mistake this site made.

badge.name: Honest hunter
badge.text: You know the difference between a candidate and a confirmed planet.

links.label: See this site's candidates and how they are labeled

steps.heading: Candidate first
body: A repeating dip is a candidate: a signal that might be a planet. It is not a discovery.
TESS's own list shows why. When we checked it on 2026-10-18, it held 4,820 planetary candidates, 815 confirmed planets and 1,315 false positives: signals that turned out not to be planets.

facts.text: The TESS Objects of Interest list marks each signal as a planetary candidate (PC), confirmed planet (CP), known planet (KP), false positive (FP) or other.

source.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive: TESS Objects of Interest table columns

checks.quote: FP =false positive KP =known planet PC =planetary candidate

steps.heading: What it takes to confirm
body: To list a planet, the NASA Exoplanet Archive needs enough follow-up observations that a false positive is unlikely.

facts.text: The NASA Exoplanet Archive requires enough follow-up observations and validation that a false positive is unlikely.

source.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive: Exoplanet Criteria for Inclusion in the Archive

checks.quote: Sufficient follow-up observations and validation have been undertaken to deem the possibility of the object being a false positive as unlikely.

steps.heading: A mistake on this site
body: Mistakes happen, and the honest thing is to fix them in the open. Two stars on this site were listed under the wrong TOI numbers. When the scan engine cross-matched each star by its TIC ID, the names did not fit: TIC 307210830 is TOI 175, not TOI 776.
Both stars are now renamed and marked unreviewed until a person checks them again. Every result here is a candidate signal that needs professional follow-up, never a discovery.

facts.text: TIC 307210830 was listed as TOI 776 by mistake; it is TOI 175.

source.name: Planet Hunter: the TOI 175 candidate page and its correction note

checks.quote: this star was listed as TOI 776 by mistake. Its TIC ID, 307210830, is TOI 175 (L 98-59).
